出海战略咨询公司美讯创始人彭家荣，是一位加拿大人，在中国求学、生活、创业已有二十年，一口地道的中文让他成为标准的“国际友人”。然而，回忆起生活中的醪糟事，他总有些“滔滔不绝”。
EN: Chris Pereira, founder of iMpact, a strategy consultancy for companies going global, is a Canadian who has studied, lived and built a business in China for twenty years. His fluent, idiomatic Chinese makes him a textbook "international friend." Yet when he recalls the frustrating episodes of daily life, he always has plenty to say.

有一次，他在上海出差，准备打一辆网约车，结果被毫无征兆地告知，他的国外信用卡使用次数已到30次，在平台无法支付。没有提前通知，也没法办理中国信用卡，他顿时陷入了被动的境地。最后的解决办法是，走一大段路，坐地铁。
EN: Once, on a business trip in Shanghai, he tried to book a ride-hailing car, only to be told without warning that his foreign credit card had reached its limit of 30 uses and could no longer be used for payment on the platform. There was no advance notice, and he could not get a Chinese credit card, so he was suddenly stuck. In the end, his only option was to walk a long way and take the subway.

EN: Although AI plays an important role in improving efficiency and polishing product image, building cross-cultural trust is still human work that AI cannot replace. Communication and trust between people are the key to a company's success overseas.
中国改革开放以来，中国出海产业持续升级，从以中低端产品和出口贸易阶段，逐步迈向定制化、个性化以及高端化的发展路径。工业文明的演进背后，是产业升级所带来的新挑战，在海外市场，在追求高端高质量发展的过程中，需要一个与之相匹配的高端形象，品牌和形象的提升显得尤为重要。
EN: Since China's reform and opening up, its globalizing industries have kept upgrading, moving step by step from low- and mid-end products and export trade toward customization, personalization and the high end. Behind the evolution of industrial civilization are new challenges brought by industrial upgrading. In overseas markets, the pursuit of high-end, high-quality development requires a matching high-end image, which makes upgrading the brand and image especially important.
许多人认为品牌是一个较为抽象的概念，然而 品牌实际上是与个人之间在文化上的共鸣，“他们觉得你是自己人、有心人”。在海外可以明显地看到一个趋势，即中国各行各业的产品和服务价值已经达到世界级水平，足以竞争得过欧美、南美等地区的产品和服务竞争。
EN: Many people think of a brand as a rather abstract concept, but a brand is actually cultural resonance with individuals: "they feel you are one of them, someone who cares." Overseas, there is a clear trend: the value of Chinese products and services across industries has reached world-class levels, good enough to compete with products and services from Europe, the Americas, South America and other regions.
当前中国企业出海面临很多问题，问题源于人与人之间的信任建立。各行各业在海外的进程中，产品好仅占成功因素的50%，而另一半则取决于海外客户对企业的喜好程度，但这对于中国企业而言都是机会。因为产品品质这一最大难题已基本解决，接下来在海外的关键就在于构建文化层面的信任。
EN: Chinese companies going global currently face many problems, and these problems stem from building trust between people. For every industry going overseas, a good product accounts for only 50% of success. The other half depends on how much overseas customers like the company. But this is an opportunity for Chinese companies. Because product quality, the biggest challenge, has largely been solved, the key overseas from here is building trust at the cultural level.
以人工智能、新能源、医疗健康和餐饮连锁四大最具代表性的行业为例。在科技领域，包括人工智能、软件即服务（SaaS）平台以及消费电子产品，在海外市场拥有巨大的潜力。其次是新能源行业，目前无论是在国内还是国际市场上，新能源汽车都备受瞩目，海外市场尤其广阔。第三是医疗智能健康领域，最后则是餐饮连锁行业，中国菜在全球范围内一直受到广泛的关注和支持。所以这四个领域是产业升级、品牌升级在海外重点机会所在。
EN: Take the four most representative industries: artificial intelligence, new energy, healthcare and restaurant chains. In technology, including artificial intelligence, software as a service (SaaS) platforms and consumer electronics, there is huge potential in overseas markets. Next is the new energy industry. New energy vehicles are drawing great attention both in China and internationally, and the overseas market is especially vast. Third is smart healthcare, and last is restaurant chains, as Chinese food has long enjoyed wide attention and support around the world. So these four fields are where the key overseas opportunities for industrial upgrading and brand upgrading lie.

Chris Pereira, former public relations manager at Huawei and now founder and CEO of business consulting group iMpact, told Nikkei Asia that the downsizing was expected.

He said Huawei North America had two main goals -- the release of Meng and achieving a breakthrough in the U.S. market. Meng was released back to China in 2021, while the latter goal now seems impossible and may even be unnecessary, he said.

"Looking at their revenue, the U.S. and Canada are actually not important for Huawei," Pereira said. "I think from the business perspective, my prediction is Huawei will focus more on the Middle East, Southeast Asia, maybe South America and Eastern Europe."

At the same time, cutting costs also made sense for the company, he added.

"The business pressure [in China] is probably quite high right now in terms of maintaining revenue and profit, so they're probably looking for ways to cut costs," Pereira said.
China's slump pushes its smaller companies overseas for growth

Chris Pereira, founder and CEO of the business consulting group iMpact, said companies in the consumer tech, new energy and biotechnology sectors are particularly prominent in the overseas sales push.

"What is actually happening is Chinese brands and companies are learning how to localize in overseas markets, from branding to team building," he said.

"The most important trend that we are seeing is China's industrial base is upgrading to a level that is competitive with Western brands and products. So the main thing is, it's not Western companies going to China to procure products, it's Chinese companies making the product and they're managing the brand and selling the product overseas by cutting out the middleman," Pereira said.

He also pointed to a number of hurdles, however.

"Fair treatment, geopolitical tensions, true localization and cross-cultural management, and marketing strategies in a different market are all the big challenges for Chinese companies operating overseas, particularly in the U.S.," he said.
